name: Higashiyama Niseko Village, a Ritz Carlton Reserve
positioning: Ritz-Carlton Reserve mountain resort in Niseko, Hokkaido, with rooms facing Mount Yotei or Niseko Annupuri, an onsen and a spa
best_for: Skiers who want a base at the foot of Mount Annupuri with gondola access
Guests who want an onsen, a spa and a dedicated Do San contact
Families wanting a kids club and interconnecting suites

facts.text: The hotel is at 919-28 Aza Soga, Niseko cho, Abuta gun, Niseko, Hokkaido, Japan.
Floor-to-ceiling windows in the rooms and suites look out over Mount Yotei or Niseko Annupuri.
Guest bathrooms are inspired by the local onsen tradition, with an oversized soaking tub, a separate rainforest shower and a large window with a mountain view.
Yukibana is an all-day restaurant overlooking Mount Yotei, with locally sourced ingredients and a farm-to-table concept.
Ume Lounge has a fireplace and serves classic cocktails customised by an alpine mixologist.
The onsen has hot indoor and outdoor baths, separate for ladies and gentlemen, with tranquil gardens and saunas.
The hotel sits at the base of Mount Annupuri, with gondola access to the slopes.
Summer activities include hiking, cycling and horseback riding.
Two 18-hole golf courses are near the resort.
The Niseko Village Kids Club welcomes children aged 1.5 to 9 years.

highlights.text: A Do San, meaning person of Hokkaido, joins each guest as a single point of contact.
The hotel's Higashiyama Reservists, a team of mountain experts, create curated ski adventures.
Spa Chasi La Sothys blends Japanese tradition with French techniques and has private onsens.
Sushi Nagi serves omakase-style sushi, with menus featuring local seafood and farm-sourced ingredients.
Seven of the suites can be interconnected to adjacent rooms for larger family groups.

considerations.text: The closest airport is New Chitose Airport in Sapporo, about 113.8 km from the hotel.
Pets are not allowed at the hotel.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing reflecting Reserve-level positioning.
